reasons.A: Clean front matter (description 138 chars, starts with 'Kimi K2', https link), no body H1, $$-only math, claim-style H2s. Deductions: L36 heading promises '세 가지 병목' while L38/L44 describe two; L265 wraps part of a display formula in {% raw %} and mixes '\mid' (numerator) with '|' (denominator); L192 '남은 과제는 뒤의 한계 절에서 다룹니다.' is a one-line stub paragraph.
reasons.B: Natural 입니다-register Korean with few stock patterns (1x '할 수 있습니다'). Minor: L32 joins a who-benefits judgement and the LMSYS fact in one bullet; L100 'Muon은 토큰 효율이 높은 옵티마이저(optimizer)입니다' adds a needless gloss.
reasons.C: Mostly smooth, with an airline example threaded L42 -> L224 -> L228 -> L413. Deductions: heading/body mismatch L36 vs L38; explicit deferrals 'L271 ... 이 장치들은 이 글에서 다루지 않습니다' and L192 leave gaps; L254 ends a subsection on the critic init with no follow-through (critic refinement never described).
reasons.D: Good help on hard parts: per-head QK-Clip worked example (L124), MLA component scaling reason (L121), objective worked example with e^0.5 (L269), pass@k zero-variance example (L248). Under-explained: why soft-cap/QK-Norm are insufficient (L102 offers generic alternatives instead of the paper's MLA argument), what the core/prescriptive rubrics are (L252), Muon itself (L100).
reasons.E: 11 figures placed where discussed and described, tables verbatim (L54-64, L182-186, L343-349, L363-369). Deductions: L323-329 '비교 모델' column packs several models and scores into prose cells; L343 drops the Claude Sonnet 4 column without saying so.
reasons.F: 2 wrong of 28 sampled claims: L379 'K2는 어려운 프롬프트 승률 54.5% ... 두 항목 모두 최고 성적' contradicts Table 3 (Claude Opus 4 59.7 on Hard Prompt; the paper's prose overclaims, the post repeats it); L387 labels the Chinese in-house win rates '무승부 제외' although the paper reports plain win rates (65.4% win with ~17% loss implies ties are included). One unsupported framing at L102 (alternatives 'loss regularization term' not in the paper).
reasons.R1: Covers architecture, MuonClip, rephrasing, agentic data, a slice of RL, FP8 storage, checkpoint engine and evaluations. Missing large parts of the paper: training infrastructure and parallelism (2.4), pre-training recipe/LR schedule/YaRN, RL domains (instruction following, faithfulness, coding/SWE, safety), closed-loop critic refinement, rubric content, budget control/PTX/temperature decay (explicitly skipped L271), tool-call template, startup/agentic rollout, safety red-team eval, 12.7%/70k-step QK-Clip statistic, 9B/53B logit-explosion evidence, appendix hypothesis.
reasons.R2: Where it goes deep it layers well (intuition -> formula -> numeric example for QK-Clip and the K1.5 objective). Length (~23k chars) is short for a 1T-parameter tech report; difficulty-heavy parts (infra, RL details) are cut rather than layered.
reasons.R3: TL;DR answers the four questions with setting-qualified numbers ('비사고 설정', L30-31). Closing (L409-417) is the writer's own judgement, separates its inference from the paper ('논문이 직접 내린 진단은 아닙니다', L413), names concrete limits (non-thinking-only comparison, in-house Chinese benchmark) and when to use K2.

reasons.A: Valid front matter (description 131 chars, https links), $$-only math, Liquid wrapped in {% raw %} (L452-466). Deductions: L34-50 '## Kimi K2 개요' is an intro section right after the TL;DR that restates the TL;DR numbers; L840-842 '### 결론부의 요약' restates the paper's conclusion; several topic headings ('L52 사전 지식: ...', 'L600 RL 알고리즘: ...', 'L736 Kimi-K2-Instruct 평가: ...'); 86 headings make the post sprawling.
reasons.B: Natural Korean, consistent terms, good register. Deductions: 9x '할 수 있습니다' including cases that simply happen; '논씽킹' transliteration where '비사고' or 'non-thinking' would read better (L28, L46); some long stacked sentences (L767, L777).
reasons.C: Background (Muon, MoE/MLA) introduced before use and referred back accurately ('앞서 본 로짓 식', L150; '앞서 설명한 PP·EP·ZeRO-1', L654). Deductions: overview section duplicates TL;DR so the reader meets the same 8 numbers three times (L28-29, L50, L756-777); architecture table appears after MuonClip although MLA was already introduced, causing some back-and-forth.
reasons.D: Excellent help on hard parts: RMS matching derivation with 1024x4096 example (L74), why QK-Norm fails on MLA (L88, L104), per-head vs naive clip numeric example (L146), alpha interpretation (L156), effective-rank and 2x2 toy examples (L201, L221), K1.5 objective worked example (L628), closed-loop critic scenario (L572). Deductions for padding the easy: AdamW primer (L58), InstructGPT 3-step RLHF (L525), Gym reset/step (L734), red-teaming and few-shot definitions (L805, L815).
reasons.E: 18 figures each introduced with what to look at; tables verbatim with stated omissions (L765 'Gemini 2.5 Flash 열은 생략', L836 '일부 행만 옮겼습니다'); tool template code is the paper's (L438-466); math used where it clarifies. Minor: two adjacent t-SNE figures (L398-400) with one shared sentence.
reasons.F: 0 wrong, 2 unsupported, 1 unverifiable of 39 sampled claims. L838 'Criminal·Privacy·Security의 프롬프트 인젝션과 반복 탈옥 일부 조합에서 K2는 다른 모델보다 통과율이 낮습니다' overgeneralizes and conflicts with its own table L831 (DeepSeek-R1 69.70 < K2 75.76) and Table 6 (Criminal-IJ K2 highest 57.57). L848 '저자들은 후속 릴리스에서 이 문제들을 해결...' extends the paper's future-release pledge (Sec 5 limitations only) to every issue listed. L46 '8개 벤치마크' figure unverifiable from text. Notably corrects two paper-prose overclaims against Table 3 (L777 GPQA vs Opus 74.9, L791 Arena-Hard second to Opus 59.7).
reasons.R1: Near-complete section-by-section coverage: MuonClip incl. appendix hypothesis and 12.7%/70k statistic, data rephrasing, architecture, parallelism/EP/activation memory, LR recipe, SFT and tool template/enforcer, every RL domain, self-critique with rubrics and critic refinement, budget/PTX/temperature, RL infra incl. startup and partial rollout, full instruct/base/safety evaluations.
reasons.R2: Consistent intuition -> formula -> worked example layering on every hard mechanism. Deduction: length (~57k chars) overshoots; easy background is padded at the same depth as hard parts.
reasons.R3: TL;DR is concrete and scoped (L25, L28-30). Closing (L844-850) has a real assessment with specific gaps (ablation only at 0.5B/tau=30, no 1T AdamW comparison, H800-specific choices) and use guidance tied to numbers (43.90, MRCR 55.0). Deductions: the closing re-lists the paper's limitations at length, L848 stretches the future-work claim, and L840-842 restates the paper's conclusion.

A.reason: X follows the TL;DR -> reader-question shape without intro or conclusion-recap sections; Y adds both and many topic headings.

B.reason: Both natural; X has fewer stock patterns and no transliteration like '논씽킹'.

C.reason: X has a heading/body mismatch and explicit deferrals; Y has repeated numbers and duplicated overview.

D.reason: Y explains the genuinely hard parts (RMS matching, QK-Norm vs MLA, critic loop) that X skips, despite some padding.

E.reason: Y's tables are verbatim with stated omissions; X packs several models into prose cells.

F.reason: Y: 0 wrong / 2 unsupported in 39 (5.3%) and it corrects the paper's prose overclaims; X: 2 wrong / 1 unsupported in 28 (10.7%), repeating one of those overclaims.

R2.reason: Both layer well; Y layers every hard mechanism, X cuts hard parts instead of layering them.

R3.reason: X's closing is a tighter own judgement with inference labelled; Y's mixes recap and a stretched future-work claim.

overall.reason: Y wins on depth and factual accuracy, the higher-stakes criteria; X is cleaner and better shaped but thinner and less accurate.
